name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Lifecycle: /spec:genesis (greenfield) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → /spec:run (design when due, then build, then review, each driver-stepped with one fresh-context reviewer and a derived verdict) → /spec:release; plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.142.0 — A repo's test count is now instrumented, not capped. `lib/scan-test-calls.js` is the one definition of a test case — a `test(`/`it(` call at line start across the host's test-classified files, blind to strings, comments and regex literals — and `count-tests.js` reports it (`tests: <count> cases`, `--json` → `{"count":N}`, never a non-zero exit for the count itself). The review's new `tests` leg records that count on every evidence manifest and is deliberately absent from every blocking set (`BLOCKING`, `REVIEW_BLOCKING`, `BLOCKING_LEGS`), so the number lands on each ledger row and can never redden a verdict. There is no limit, no ceiling file and no hook: `spec/test-ceiling.json` is deleted, and a count that could fail a build would make deleting tests the model's cheapest route to green. 7.141.0 — The escape command's prevention-note step no longer prescribes the escape row's own id as a Gotchas entry's owner citation. That id embeds a timestamp, and the same sentence bans dates in exactly that section, so every entry written to the old instruction was classed as date narration and reddened the repo-wide narration scan. The step now prescribes the spec path the defect escaped plus the spec that fixes it, and says outright that the row id is never the citation. 7.140.0 — The client player's own chrome is now English-only: the two-language STRINGS table and the lang role are retired from lib/walk-page.js and design-atlas.js's clientRoute, closing an escaped defect where the page declared <html lang="en"> while rendering Japanese chrome. Every save on the player now acts only on the server's answer — a mark hides, the open count drops, a note clears or a reached label counts only once the server responds ok, and any refusal or network failure leaves the page unchanged and reports it in a new [data-wk="msg"] status slot instead of guessing ahead of the network. POST /client/__walk/confirm independently refuses with 409 while any question anchored to the journey's screens is unanswered, so a stale tab or a failed player script can no longer record a client sign-off over an open question.
